reference: Contract expectations use Bash's documented type/help builtins and the pinned mkfs help text. There is no GNU formatter with matching behavior; e2fsprogs mke2fs is an independent ext2 implementation but has different defaults and on-disk output, so it is not used as a byte-for-byte parity oracle.
coverage: Bash reports mkfs as an available builtin.
The builtin's concise help description and synopsis match its documented interface.
Deferred regular-image cases specify ext2 layout, options, dry-run, and input-validation checks for a future authorized fixture run.
A deferred block-device case specifies the mock or disposable-VM requirement for BLKGETSIZE64 and I/O error behavior.
exclusions: No formatter operation was invoked, per the instruction not to run dangerous loadables.
No real block device, loop device, mount, mounted filesystem, power-loss test, or maximum-capacity image is in scope.
No mke2fs comparison is labeled GNU parity; it is a different implementation with non-identical defaults and artifacts.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must identify the registered mkfs loadable as a builtin.
Bash type must describe the registered command as a shell builtin.
The short help description must match the first line of the builtin's documented help text.
cases.stdout: mkfs - Create a minimal ext2 filesystem on IMAGE.

cases.purpose: The concise help synopsis must expose the documented operand and supported options.
cases.stdout: mkfs: mkfs IMAGE [-L LABEL] [-b BLOCKSIZE] [-m PCT] [-F] [-n]

cases.purpose: Verify successful formatting of a small relative regular-file image with default options and each supported block size, including filesystem geometry and the root/lost+found directories.
cases.reason: Requires explicit authorization to invoke the destructive formatter on per-case fixture images in a disposable VM or isolated fixture runner. A future run must use only small relative images, independently decode ext2 fields and directory records, and check the results with available read-only tools such as e2fsck -fn, dumpe2fs, debugfs, and blkid.

cases.purpose: Check -L truncation at 16 bytes, -m boundaries, -F compatibility, -- option termination, and preservation of the regular image's length across supported block sizes.
cases.reason: Requires the same explicit authorization and disposable fixture environment as regular-image formatting. The expected label, reserved-block count, block size, image length, and ext2 features must be derived from the documented contract and an independent ext2 decoder, not from candidate output.

cases.purpose: Check that -n leaves a prefilled relative image byte-for-byte unchanged and that malformed options, undersized images, and layouts too small for metadata fail without changing image contents.
cases.reason: The loadable must not be invoked under the current safety instruction. A future disposable fixture run should hash the small image before and after, cover documented status classes and representative numeric boundaries, and keep all paths relative to the private fixture directory.

cases.purpose: Exercise BLKGETSIZE64 sizing and bounded write, sync, and close failures without touching a host device.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a dedicated disposable block device or a separately reviewed syscall mock that redirects every write to a test-owned regular image. The mock must inject ioctl and I/O failures and verify recovery and descriptor cleanup; no physical or host block device may be used.
